argv: Cold adversarial review, read-only. Repository: this workspace, branch p357-power-sim. Review commit 03422ebc (git show 03422ebc): the P357 fix of benchmark/m64/power_sim.py (docs/open-questions.md entries P357, P347, C168; the bug was found in benchmark/chains/c147/reviews/m65/p356-round1.cursor-gpt-5.6-sol-high.md finding S4: old sim_cell symmetrically flipped a fixed high-accuracy reference, so true Δ=0 simulated about -3.7 pp at r=.955 — confirmed by the lead: -3.69 pp at r=.955, -4.12 pp at r=1.0). The fix replaces sim_cell with joint_table/feasible_ref/sim_pairs; feasible_ref CLAMPS each cell's reference accuracy to the nearest feasible value (e.g. 1 - p_d/2 at Δ=0). POWER_SIM.md was regenerated; new results include pooled power at Δ=0, p_d .041 = 0.49–0.51 (was 0.30–0.34) and a pooled FALSE-PASS rate at Δ=-5 pp, p_d .050 of 0.16–0.18 (was 0.000). Check: (1) correctness of the joint table and sampling (E[delta]=Δ, discordance split, marginals, per-cell n discreteness); (2) whether clamping the reference accuracy is a sound modelling choice or distorts the scenario relative to the real references (c144-base / P223 rows) — propose a better alternative if not; (3) the 0.16–0.18 false-pass at the margin: is it a simulation artifact (e.g. boundary case p_d = |Δ| meaning every discordance is one-sided, clamping) or a genuine anti-conservatism of the repo's decision rule (benchmark/bench/stats.py paired_delta / the TOST p-value in power_sim.py, percentile bootstrap at the margin)? If genuine, state the consequence for decisions made with stats.paired_delta and the fix; (4) test adequacy (benchmark/bench/tests/test_p357_power_sim.py) — the red-first evidence was only AttributeError on missing functions, so say what a behavioural regression test should assert; (5) whether P347's corrected text in open-questions is accurate. Numbered findings Q1..Qn with severity, file:line, failure scenario, fix; final line exactly one of 'VERDICT: CLEARED', 'VERDICT: CLEARED AFTER FIXES <ids>', 'VERDICT: NOT CLEARED'.
